Today's update focuses on game optimization and improvements to graphics settings, including options related to DLSS and FSR.

Optimized the vehicle mask system and the way its associated data is stored. This system handles a large amount of information related to vehicle washing, dirt levels, rust, and more. Since it accounts for a significant amount of data stored in RAM and save files, optimizing it was particularly important.
Improved the DLSS and FSR presets, verified their functionality, and added more configuration options. You can find them under Settings > Graphics.

Resolved conflicts between graphics settings and improved how they work together. This includes options related to Global Illumination (GI) and Reflections, making it easier to fine-tune the game's visuals to your preferences.
Improved anti-aliasing when using TSR, providing smoother edges and reducing unwanted visual artifacts.
Rebuilt the HLOD system across the map to improve the rendering of distant objects and reduce system load while exploring the game world.

Alongside fixing bugs and working on new content, part of our team is continuously working on game optimization. The results of their work will be gradually introduced in upcoming updates. Be sure to follow our devlogs to stay up to date with what we're working on for you!

notes.title: From now on, vehicles have three fluid reservoirs

items.text: engine oil
coolant
brake fluid
Fluids are consumed while driving. A low fluid level causes the related part to wear out faster, while running completely out of fluid makes the vehicle unsafe to drive.
The vehicle HUD indicators will let you know when a fluid level is low. You can also check the fluid levels using the scanner.
Fluids can be purchased both at the physical store and through the online shop.
A new fluid-related minigame has been added to repair mode. The UI shows the current fluid level in the reservoir, as well as the amount of fluid remaining in the bottle.
Filling the fluid works similarly to loosening wheel bolts - hold the left mouse button and drag down along the indicator to tilt the bottle and refill the fluid.
Both the mechanic employee and the automation platform now account for fluid replacement in their tasks and display it in their respective UIs.
Fluid replacement and low fluid levels become available once you unlock the ability to replace the parts associated with them.

There are ways to slightly deceive your customers about the condition of the vehicles you’re selling.
Instead of replacing exhaust system parts, you can... patch them up with tape. This improves their condition, while your customers have no idea what’s really going on underneath.

In Car Dealer Simulator, you have several trailers and specialized vehicles at your disposal:
Tow Dolly - allows you to tow damaged vehicles.

Fuel Dolly - allows you to transport larger amounts of fuel to your dealership. This lets you sell vehicles with a full tank, ready to hit the road. Customers really appreciate this, and it’s reflected in your reputation.

Tow Truck - a special vehicle that makes transporting cars much easier. It also has an upgrade that allows you to transport two vehicles at the same time! Here’s a little pro tip - you can connect the Car Transporter with a Tow Dolly, allowing you to tow up to three vehicles at once.

Transporter - a large truck that, together with its trailer, can transport up to 7 vehicles. You can also hire an employee to operate the Transporter, making vehicle trading even easier and allowing you to scale up your business.

notes.title: Phantom Ravager - available from Reputation Level 15

items.text: The Ravager, launched in late 1990, was initially met with a lukewarm response from the automotive community. Inspired by the iconic American muscle cars of the 1960s and 1970s, its retro styling, premium price tag, and uncompromising V8-powered design made it a difficult sell at first. However, positive word-of-mouth, a successful marketing campaign, and a memorable appearance in a blockbuster movie gradually helped the Ravager find its audience.

Over time, the Ravager earned a reputation for performance, reliability, and safety, becoming one of Phantom's greatest success stories. Today, it is widely regarded as one of the finest vehicles ever produced by the company and remains a favorite among enthusiasts around the world.

In today's update, we're expanding the Pawn Shop and giving it a whole new purpose!

After the recent economy update some of you noticed that profits on vehicles bought before the patch may look different than expected. Let us quickly explain why.
Before the update, vehicles in the game used a different market value system. The new economy introduced updated vehicle values and a new way of calculating service labor.
Because of that, vehicles purchased before the patch may behave differently depending on their original price.
What does this mean in practice?
Cheaper vehicles from before the update may now have a higher market value, which means you can actually earn a bit more on them.
More expensive vehicles may now have a lower market value, so selling them immediately could result in a loss.
If you want to minimize potential losses on older vehicles, you can replace some parts again (even if they are already at 100%). The labor cost will then be added to the vehicle value.
Newly purchased vehicles already use the updated economy system, so this mismatch will not occur.
We’re sorry for the inconvenience. As you know, we’re constantly working to improve the game for you, and sometimes changes like this aren’t easy to implement without side effects.

A big economy update is here, preparing the game for the upcoming Up 2 You DLC. This is another step in developing systems that will support new mechanical parts and even deeper gameplay in the future.
1. Parts now directly affect vehicle value
From now on, the price of parts directly translates into the value of the car.
Part value = base price × durability.
This makes the calculations clearer and more intuitive.
2. Labor now matters
Your work is now also included in the vehicle’s price.
Each part replacement has a service cost that increases the vehicle’s value.
Service cost scales with the value of the car.
Better car = higher labor value.
3. Better balancing between vehicle tiers
The same part can appear in both early-tier and late-tier vehicles.
From now on, labor cost balances the difference and better reflects the class of the vehicle.
The changes have been thoroughly tested across multiple scenarios.
The average profit per vehicle has not changed.
However, market values have been adjusted.
That’s why it’s worth checking your current listings and making sure the prices are still attractive to customers.
Some vehicles listed on the marketplace may now have a lower price than before the update.
This creates a clearer, more scalable, and future-proof economy system.

We see that many of you have reported issues with negotiations, so we would like to clarify a few things.

There were no changes to the core negotiation system. The limitations applied only to the Non-Negotiable option and to customers who automatically accepted the price without negotiating. These limits were introduced because vehicles could be sold with no price restrictions and this was being used as a money glitch.

We improved the attractiveness bar behavior. When switching the price to Non-Negotiable, you can now check whether customers will be interested at all. The lower the bar fill, the longer the wait for a customer. This has always worked this way.

Market Value is an average market price that takes into account the vehicle’s age, mileage, and technical condition. It is not an indicator of profit or loss, but only a guideline for the price at which you can sell the vehicle.

The difference between the purchase price and your total investment, including replaced parts, is visible on the scanner. It is also displayed in the negotiation window next to Purchase Price. Green indicates profit, red indicates loss compared to the original purchase price.
We are working on improving the clarity of the negotiation window and plan to introduce changes that will make it easier to navigate.

Introduced in 2006, the Summit combined the strength of a pickup with the practicality of an SUV. With a large open bed and four doors for driver and passengers, it was built for those who needed both cargo space and everyday comfort. Its sturdy suspension, high ground clearance, and solid construction made it just as capable on worksites as it was on weekend off-road adventures.

Even after production ended in 2010, the Summit remains valued for its versatility and reliability, proving that a vehicle can deliver the toughness of a truck while offering the convenience of a family-friendly layout.

items.text: In one of our recent devlogs we showed a preview of a new device. The air compressor. Today we explain what this change brings to the gameplay loop.

items.text: Today, we’ll focus on what you’ll be able to sell at the junkyard - and we’ll reveal more new features in the next devlog.
First of all, you’ll now be able to sell non-functional vehicles at the junkyard.

As you might remember, it was already possible to sell such cars from your Car Dealer lot - but doing so would cost you reputation points. If you have broken cars with missing parts and don’t want to repair them, now you can sell them safely at the junkyard without losing reputation.

The junkyard owner has lower expectations than regular customers - but there’s no haggling involved. After driving onto a specially marked area, the vehicle will be evaluated and you’ll decide whether or not to sell it. The final price will depend on the installed parts and their condition, as well as how much rust is covering the car.

You’ll also be able to sell stripped, incomplete wrecks. If you’re buying cars just to reuse the parts in other vehicles, the junkyard is the best place to get rid of the empty shell. You can then refurbish the removed parts using the restoration machine you already know from the warehouse, and use them to repair other vehicles.

issues.text: Some players reported a bug where meeting locations would spawn outside the city. This issue was caused by the removal of a point on the map.
